text:
alex: Heads up — nightly e2e run e2e-runner-197 failed perf gate at 03:12 UTC. p95 is fine but p99 latency jumped ~2.1x for longseq. Suspect runner queue delays.
mira: saw a similar spike on canary yesterday, might be autoscaler churn or a slow node.
alex: logs show repeated queue wait spikes from the runner queue. excerpt:
```
[03:11:59] worker-42: dequeue start
[03:12:00] worker-42: queue_wait_ms=1248
[03:12:01] worker-42: start exec
[03:12:02] request-id=abcd1234 p99=1.2s
```
tyler: can someone /ci rerun that job and collect the runner queue metrics (+ kube events)?
ci-bot: /ci rerun e2e-runner-197 --target longseq — rerun queued (job 197-rerun-1). I'll post results when done.
alex: thanks. @sre-bot @jamie can you check autoscaler logs around 03:10-03:13? if nodes were cycling that would explain queueing.
sre-bot: looking now — noticed a single node marked NotReady at 03:09 followed by pod reschedules. attaching brief events snippet:
```
03:09:18 node/node-7 NotReady Kubelet stopped heartbeat
03:09:25 pod/runner-xyz Killing container, reason: eviction
03:11:50 pod/runner-xyz Started container
```
mira: eviction/reschedule window matches the p99 spike. maybe warmup for new instances wasn't completed before test traffic.
tyler: suggest we tag this as flaky infra-induced and bisect only if rerun reproduces. if rerun still fails with no node churn, then bisect code changes.
alex: agreed. If rerun passes, we'll mark as infra and close. If it fails consistently, I'll open a bisect request and ping infra owners.
ci-bot: rerun finished: 197-rerun-1 — PASS for latency gate but small throughput dip. p99 back to baseline.
alex: ok passing on rerun, marking as infra-related. I'll follow up with infra to get root cause and ask for node health alert tuning. :thumbsup:
jamie: filing a follow-up ticket with node metrics and kube events, linking this thread.
